\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Signed literal]
\lean{FABL.Literal}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004
}
\label{FABL.Literal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a positive integer $n$, a literal on $n$ Boolean variables consists of a coordinate
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a required sign $s\in\{-1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Literal evaluation]
\lean{FABL.Literal.eval}
\label{FABL.Literal.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
For a dimension $n$, let a literal specify a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a
required sign $r\in\{\pm1\}$. On an input $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, its value is $-1$ if
$x_i=r$, and $+1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Literal evaluation criterion]
\lean{FABL.Literal.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.Literal.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal, FABL.Literal.eval}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a literal specify a coordinate $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and a required sign $s\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^{n}$ be a sign vector. The
literal evaluates to $-1$ exactly when $x_i=s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Negation of a literal]
\lean{FABL.Literal.negate}
\label{FABL.Literal.negate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
For a dimension $n$, negating a literal preserves its coordinate and replaces its
required sign $r\in\{\pm1\}$ by $-r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[DNF term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b004}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004
}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Literal}
For $n$ variables, a DNF term is a finite list of signed literals whose coordinate
indices are pairwise distinct.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Term width]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b002
}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm}
The width of a DNF term is the number of literals in its list.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Term evaluation]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eval}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal.eval, FABL.Sign}
For a dimension $n$, let a term be a finite list of literals with pairwise distinct
coordinates. On an input $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, its value is $-1$ exactly when every listed
literal has value $-1$, and is $+1$ otherwise; in particular, the empty term has value
$-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[When a term evaluates to minus one]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.Literal.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates, with no coordinate appearing
more than once, and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. The term evaluates to $-1$ at $x$ if and only
if every literal in $T$ requires the sign that $x$ has at its coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empty term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.empty}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm}
For any dimension $n$, the empty term is the term with no literals.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the empty term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.width_empty}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.width_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.empty, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\difficulty{1}
For every number $n$ of coordinates, the empty DNF term has width $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the empty term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_empty}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.empty, FABL.DNFTerm.eval}
\difficulty{1}
For every dimension $n$ and every sign vector $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, the empty conjunction
evaluates to $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Two-literal term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.pair}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.pair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Sign}
For a dimension $n$, choose distinct coordinates $i,j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and any
required signs $r,s\in\{\pm1\}$. The associated two-literal term consists, in order, of
the literal at coordinate $i$ requiring $r$ and the literal at coordinate $j$ requiring
$s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width of a two-literal term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.width_pair}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.width_pair}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.pair, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $i$ and $j$ be distinct coordinates among $n$
coordinates. For any signs $s_i,s_j\in\{-1,1\}$, the conjunction term requiring sign
$s_i$ at coordinate $i$ and sign $s_j$ at coordinate $j$ has width $2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Minterm determined by an input]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.minterm}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p034-b006}

For each sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the associated minterm contains one literal for

\begin{theorem}[Width of a minterm]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.width_minterm}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.width_minterm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.minterm, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\difficulty{1}
For every input $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, the minterm specifying the value of $x$ at each

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a minterm]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_minterm_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_minterm_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.minterm}
\difficulty{4}
For sign vectors $x,y\in\{\pm1\}^n$, the minterm specifying the signs of $x$ evaluates

\begin{definition}[Term support]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.support}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm}
For a dimension $n$, the support of a term is the set of coordinates appearing among its
literals.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Support size equals term width]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.card_support}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.card_support}
\leanok

Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ Boolean coordinates, with distinct
coordinates in its literals. The cardinality of the set of coordinates appearing in $T$

\begin{theorem}[Width bounded by dimension]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension}
\leanok

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Number of terms]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.size}

\begin{definition}[Maximum term width]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.width}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{

}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on a running maximum]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.foldl_max_le}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.foldl_max_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $B \in \mathbb{N}$. For
any finite list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$ and initial value $a \in \mathbb{N}$, if
$f(t) \le B$ for every $t \in L$ and $a \le B$, then the value obtained by folding the
operation $(u,t) \mapsto \max(u,f(t))$ over $L$, starting from $a$, is at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The running maximum bounds its initial value]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max_aux}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max_aux}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, let $a \in \mathbb{N}$, and let
$L$ be any finite list of elements of $\alpha$. Folding $(u,b) \mapsto \max(u,f(b))$
over $L$, starting from $a$, produces a value at least $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A list element is bounded by the running maximum]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max_aux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, and let $L$ be a finite list of
elements of $\alpha$. For any initial value $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $t \in L$, the
value $f(t)$ is at most the result of folding $(u,b) \mapsto \max(u,f(b))$ over $L$,
starting from $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Term width bounded by formula width]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_of_mem}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_of_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.le_foldl_max, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\difficulty{1}
Let a disjunctive normal form formula be a finite list of terms, each a conjunction of
literals on distinct coordinates. Every term appearing in the formula has width at most
the width of the formula, where the formula width is the maximum term width, or zero if
the formula is empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Formula width criterion]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.foldl_max_le, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_of_mem, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\difficulty{4}
Let a disjunctive normal form formula be a finite list of terms, each a conjunction of
literals on distinct coordinates, and let its width be the maximum term width (or zero
for an empty list). Its width is at most $w$ if and only if every term in the formula
has width at most $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Formula evaluation]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.eval}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.Sign}
For a dimension $n$, let a formula be a finite list of terms. On an input
$x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, its value is $-1$ exactly when at least one term has value $-1$, and
is $+1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Negative evaluation of a DNF]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign
coordinates, and let $x$ be a sign vector of length $n$. The value of $\varphi$ at $x$
is $-1$ if and only if at least one term of $\varphi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empty formula]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.empty}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula}
For any dimension $n$, the empty formula is the formula with no terms.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the empty formula]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.size_empty}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.size_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.empty, FABL.DNFFormula.size}
\difficulty{1}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the empty disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates has size
zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the empty disjunctive normal form]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.eval_empty}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.eval_empty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.empty, FABL.DNFFormula.eval}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, the
disjunctive normal form with no terms evaluates to $1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function represented by a formula]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004
}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval}
For a disjunctive normal form formula $$n, its associated Boolean function maps each
assignment in $^n$ to the sign determined by evaluating the formula on that assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Width truncation]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b001
}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
Given a disjunctive normal form formula $$n and a natural number $w$, width truncation
retains exactly those terms containing at most $w$ literals, preserving their order.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width after truncation]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.width_truncateWidth_le}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.width_truncateWidth_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff}
\difficulty{3}
Let a disjunctive normal form formula consist of terms that are conjunctions of literals
on distinct coordinates. For any natural number $w$, delete every term whose width
exceeds $w$; the resulting formula has width at most $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size does not increase under width truncation]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.size_truncateWidth_le}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.size_truncateWidth_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates, and
let $w\in\mathbb N$. The formula obtained by retaining only terms of width at most $w$
has size at most the size of $\varphi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Conjunctive normal form formula]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b004}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm}
For a natural number $n$, a conjunctive normal form formula on $n$ variables is a finite
list of clauses, each clause being a term built from literals; the formula is the
conjunction of the disjunctions of its stored literals.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Negation on the sign cube]
\lean{FABL.signCubeNegEquiv}
\label{FABL.signCubeNegEquiv}
\leanok
For each natural number $n$, the map on sign vectors of length $n$ that sends every
coordinate $x_i$ to $-x_i$ is an equivalence from the sign cube to itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Number of clauses]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.size}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.size}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula}
For a conjunctive normal form formula $$n, its size is the number of clauses in the
formula.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum clause width]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.width}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b004}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.width}
For a conjunctive normal form formula $$n, its width is the maximum number of literals
in any clause, with width $0$ when the formula has no clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clause evaluation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal.eval, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $C$ be a term of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let
$x$ be a sign vector of length $n$. The clause value is $-1$ if at least one literal in
$C$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$, and is $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Formula evaluation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.eval}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ coordinates, and let $x$
be a sign vector of length $n$. The formula value is $-1$ if every clause has value $-1$
at $x$, and is $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[CNF formula as a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.eval}
For every natural number $n$ and every conjunctive normal form formula on $n$ variables,
its associated Boolean function is the function obtained by evaluating that formula.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean dual of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p107-b008
}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
For every natural number $n$ and Boolean function $f$ on $n$ variables, its Boolean dual
sends an input $x$ to the negative of $f$ evaluated at the coordinatewise negation of
$x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of a sign]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.sign_eq_of_ne_neg}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.sign_eq_of_ne_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{4}
For signs $x,s\in\{-1,1\}$, if $x\ne -s$, then $x=s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Switching conjunctions and disjunctions]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b005}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula}
For every natural number $n$ and CNF formula on $n$ variables, the corresponding DNF
formula has exactly the same list of terms as the CNF formula has clauses.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Clause and term evaluations under negation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_neg_iff_termEval}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval_neg_iff_termEval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.clauseEval, FABL.CNFFormula.sign_eq_of_ne_neg, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.Literal.eval}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $C$ be a term on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, and let
$x$ be a point of that cube. The clause evaluation of $C$ at the coordinatewise negation
of $x$ equals $1$ if and only if the term evaluation of $C$ at $x$ equals $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Switching a CNF to its Boolean dual]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_toBooleanFunction}

  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $\{-1,1\}^n$, interpreted as a
sign-valued Boolean function $f$. Regard its clauses as terms of a DNF formula. The
resulting function at $x$ equals $-f(-x)$, where $-x$ negates every coordinate of $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function with bounded DNF size]
\lean{FABL.HasDNFSizeLE}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b002
}
\label{FABL.HasDNFSizeLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
A Boolean function on $n$ variables has DNF size at most $s$ if there is a DNF formula
representing that function whose size is at most the natural number $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function with bounded DNF width]
\lean{FABL.HasDNFWidthLE}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b002
}
\label{FABL.HasDNFWidthLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width}
A Boolean function on $n$ variables has DNF width at most $w$ if there is a DNF formula
representing that function whose width is at most the natural number $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function with bounded CNF size]
\lean{FABL.HasCNFSizeLE}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.HasCNFSizeLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction}
A Boolean function on $n$ variables has CNF size at most $s$ if there is a CNF formula
representing that function whose size is at most the natural number $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function with bounded CNF width]
\lean{FABL.HasCNFWidthLE}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b004}
\label{FABL.HasCNFWidthLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.width}
A Boolean function on $n$ variables has CNF width at most $w$ if there is a CNF formula
representing that function whose width is at most the natural number $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Minterm DNF of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.mintermDNF}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012}
\label{FABL.mintermDNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.minterm}
For every natural number $n$ and Boolean function $f$ on $n$ variables, its minterm DNF
consists of one minterm for each input $x$ at which $f(x)=-1$, with the minterm
constructed from that input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minterm DNF size bound]
\lean{FABL.size_mintermDNF_le}
\label{FABL.size_mintermDNF_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.Sign, FABL.mintermDNF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign
cube to $\\{ -1,1\\}$. The size of the minterm disjunctive normal form formed from the
inputs on which $f$ equals $-1$ is at most $2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width bound for minterm DNF]
\lean{FABL.width_mintermDNF_le}
\label{FABL.width_mintermDNF_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.width_minterm, FABL.mintermDNF}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, the width of its minterm
disjunctive normal form is at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Minterm representation of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.mintermDNF_toBooleanFunction}
\label{FABL.mintermDNF_toBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_minterm_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.minterm, FABL.mintermDNF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Form a disjunctive normal form with one minterm for each
input $x$ such that $f(x)=-1$, where that minterm is satisfied exactly at $x$ and the
value $-1$ represents satisfaction. The Boolean function represented by this formula
equals $f$ at every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded DNF representation]
\lean{FABL.exists_DNFFormula_size_width_bound}
\label{FABL.exists_DNFFormula_size_width_bound}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.mintermDNF, FABL.mintermDNF_toBooleanFunction, FABL.size_mintermDNF_le, FABL.width_mintermDNF_le}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, there is a
DNF representation of $f$ with at most $2^n$ terms and width at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Every Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube has a disjunctive normal form
computing it with at most $2^n$ terms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[DNF width bound by dimension]
\lean{FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_dimension}
\label{FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.HasDNFWidthLE, FABL.exists_DNFFormula_size_width_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Every Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube has a disjunctive normal form
computing it in which each term contains at most $n$ literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Minimum DNF size]
\lean{FABL.DNFsize}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b002
}
\label{FABL.DNFsize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.HasDNFSizeLE}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, define its DNF size to
be the infimum in $\bbr$-valued notation of the natural numbers $s$ for which $f$ has a
DNF of size at most $s$; since this is an infimum in $\bbr$ over a subset of $\bbr$, it is
the greatest lower bound of those admissible sizes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Minimum DNF width]
\lean{FABL.DNFwidth}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b002
}
\label{FABL.DNFwidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.HasDNFWidthLE}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, define its DNF width to
be the infimum of the natural numbers $w$ for which $f$ has a DNF of width at most $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Attainment of minimum DNF size]
\lean{FABL.hasDNFSizeLE_DNFsize}
\label{FABL.hasDNFSizeLE_DNFsize}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFsize, FABL.HasDNFSizeLE, FABL.hasDNFSizeLE_two_pow}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, there is a disjunctive
normal form computing it whose number of terms is at most the minimum possible number of
terms among such formulas.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Attainment of minimum DNF width]
\lean{FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_DNFwidth}
\label{FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_DNFwidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DNFwidth, FABL.HasDNFWidthLE, FABL.hasDNFWidthLE_dimension}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, there is a disjunctive
normal form computing it whose width is at most the minimum possible width among such
formulas.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sign to Boolean value]
\lean{FABL.signToBit}
\label{FABL.signToBit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For a sign $s$, define its Boolean value to be true exactly when $s=-1$, and false
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three-input sorting function]
\lean{FABL.sort3}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b005
}
\label{FABL.sort3}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.signToBit}
For an input $x\in\{-1,1\}^3$, let $b_i$ be the bit corresponding to the sign $x_i$ for
$i=0,1,2$. The function takes the value $-1$ exactly when $b_0\le b_1\le b_2$ or $b_2\le
b_1\le b_0$, and takes the value $1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduced DNF for three-bit sorting]
\lean{FABL.sort3ReducedDNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b001
}
\label{FABL.sort3ReducedDNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.pair}
Consider the DNF formula on three sign-valued coordinates whose terms require,
respectively, that coordinates $0$ and $1$ both have sign $-1$, that coordinates $1$ and
$2$ both have sign $1$, or that coordinate $0$ has sign $1$ and coordinate $2$ has sign
$-1$. Each term is the conjunction of its two indicated literals, and the formula is the
disjunction of these three terms.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Four-term DNF for three-bit sorting]
\lean{FABL.sort3DNF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b008
}
\label{FABL.sort3DNF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.pair, FABL.sort3ReducedDNF}
Take the three-term DNF on three sign-valued coordinates whose terms require,
respectively, signs $(-1,-1)$ on coordinates $(0,1)$, signs $(1,1)$ on $(1,2)$, and
signs $(1,-1)$ on $(0,2)$. Append the term requiring sign $-1$ at coordinate $0$ and
sign $1$ at coordinate $2$; the resulting four-term formula is the defined DNF.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
On the three-dimensional Boolean cube, the reduced DNF function agrees pointwise with
the function that returns $-1$ when the three input bits, obtained by identifying sign
$-1$ with true and sign $1$ with false, are in nondecreasing or nonincreasing order, and
returns $1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
For inputs of three signs, let the sorting function take the value $-1$ exactly when the
corresponding bits are monotone (nondecreasing or nonincreasing), and $1$ otherwise. The
disjunctive normal form whose terms specify those monotone bit patterns computes this
function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Negative-output pivotality]
\lean{FABL.IsNegOnePivotal}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p011-b006}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p046-b002}
\label{FABL.IsNegOnePivotal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $i$ be a
coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $x$ be an input. The coordinate $i$ is
negative-output pivotal for $f$ at $x$ exactly when $f(x)=-1$ and coordinate $i$ is
pivotal for $f$ at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pivotal coordinates and term width]
\lean{FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_term_width}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003}
\label{FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_term_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.flipCoordinate, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $\{-1,1\}^n$,
and let $x$ be an input. If a term $T$ occurs in $\varphi$ and is satisfied by $x$, then
the number of coordinates whose flip changes the formula's output, when its output at
$x$ is $-1$, is at most the number of literals in $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pivotal coordinates and formula width]
\lean{FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_width}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003}
\label{FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_of_mem, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_term_width}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $\{-1,1\}^n$,
and let $x$ be an input. The number of coordinates whose flip changes the formula's
output, when its output at $x$ is $-1$, is at most the maximum number of literals in any
term of $\varphi$, taking this maximum to be zero when there are no terms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of literals by coordinate]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eq_of_mem_of_index_eq}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eq_of_mem_of_index_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a literal on $n$ coordinates consist of a
coordinate and a required sign in $\\bbz^\times$. A conjunction term is a list of such
literals whose coordinates are pairwise distinct. If two literals in the same term have
the same coordinate, then they are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Literal at a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Literal}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a term of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let
$i$ be a coordinate in the support of $T$. The selected literal at $i$ is the unique
literal in $T$ whose coordinate is $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Selected literal belongs to the term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_mem}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let $i$ belong to its
support. The literal selected at coordinate $i$ is one of the literals of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Index of the selected literal]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_index}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_index}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let $i$ belong to its
support. The literal selected at coordinate $i$ has index $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Literal coordinates lie in the support]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.mem_support_of_mem_literals}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.mem_support_of_mem_literals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Literal}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a DNF term on $n$ coordinates. The coordinate
of every literal appearing in $T$ belongs to the support of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Literal selected from its support coordinate]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_eq}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eq_of_mem_of_index_eq, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_index, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_mem, FABL.DNFTerm.mem_support_of_mem_literals, FABL.Literal}
\difficulty{1}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let $\ell$ be one of its
literals. The literal selected from the support of $T$ at coordinate $\ell$’s index is
$\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Required sign at a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.requiredAt}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.requiredAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a term of literals on $n$ coordinates, and let
$i$ belong to its support. The required sign at $i$ is the sign required by the literal
of $T$ at that coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation via required signs on the support]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff_requiredAt}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff_requiredAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_eq, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_index, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_mem, FABL.DNFTerm.mem_support_of_mem_literals, FABL.DNFTerm.requiredAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates, with no coordinate appearing
more than once, and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. The term evaluates to $-1$ at $x$ if and only
if, at every coordinate in the support of $T$, the sign of $x$ equals the sign required
by the literal at that coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinates outside the support]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.Outside}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.Outside}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.support}
For a natural number $n$ and a term $T$ of literals on $n$ coordinates, the coordinates
outside the support of $T$ are the coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ that do not belong
to that support.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Satisfying assignments and free coordinates]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.satisfyingEquiv}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.satisfyingEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.Outside, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.eval_eq_neg_one_iff_requiredAt, FABL.DNFTerm.requiredAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a term of literals on $n$ coordinates. There
is an equivalence between sign vectors satisfying $T$ and assignments of signs to the
coordinates outside the support of $T$: it sends a satisfying vector to its restriction
there, and its inverse fills coordinates in the support with their required signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Number of satisfying assignments]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.card_eval_neg_one}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.card_eval_neg_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.Outside, FABL.DNFTerm.card_support, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.satisfyingEquiv, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ Boolean coordinates, with distinct
coordinates in its literals, and let $\operatorname{width}(T)$ be its number of
literals. The number of sign assignments in $\{-1,1\}^n$ on which every literal of $T$
is true is $2^{n-\operatorname{width}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of a satisfied DNF term]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_DNFTerm_eval_neg_one}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_DNFTerm_eval_neg_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.card_eval_neg_one, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension, FABL.Sign, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on a finite sign cube, with no coordinate appearing
more than once, and let its width be the number of literals. Under the uniform
distribution on the sign cube, the probability that $T$ evaluates to $-1$ is
$2^{-\mathrm{width}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation commutes with a finite list sum]
\lean{FABL.expect_sum_list_map}
\label{FABL.expect_sum_list_map}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $l$ be a finite list
of elements of $\alpha$, and let $f\colon\alpha\to(\Omega\to\mathbb{R})$. The uniform
expectation over $x\in\Omega$ of the sum of $f(a)(x)$ over entries $a$ of $l$ equals the
sum over entries $a$ of $l$ of the uniform expectation of $f(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[DNF width truncation cutoff]
\lean{FABL.dnfWidthTruncationCutoff}
\label{FABL.dnfWidthTruncationCutoff}
\leanok
For a natural number $s$ and a real number $\varepsilon$, define the cutoff to be the
natural-number ceiling of $\log_2(s/\varepsilon)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Width cutoff reciprocal bound]
\lean{FABL.mul_inv_two_pow_dnfWidthTruncationCutoff_le}
\label{FABL.mul_inv_two_pow_dnfWidthTruncationCutoff_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.dnfWidthTruncationCutoff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s$ be a natural number and let $\varepsilon>0$. Define the width cutoff $W$ to be
the least natural number greater than or equal to $\log_2(s/\varepsilon)$. Then
$s\,2^{-W}\le\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign
coordinates, let $w\in\mathbb N$, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. If the DNF obtained from
$\varphi$ by retaining only terms of width at most $w$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$, then
$\varphi$ itself evaluates to $-1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on the Boolean cube, and let $w$ be a
nonnegative integer. If, at some input $x$, the formula and the formula obtained by
deleting all terms of width greater than $w$ have different values, then $\varphi$
contains a term of width greater than $w$ that evaluates to true at $x$.
\end{theorem}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on
$\{\pm1\}^n$ whose terms are conjunctions of literals on distinct coordinates. If its
number of terms is at most $s$, then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of inputs
on which $\varphi$ differs from the formula retaining only terms of width at most
$\lceil\log_2(s/\varepsilon)\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on the
Boolean cube $\{\pm1\}^n$, with each term a conjunction of literals on distinct
coordinates. For every $\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of inputs on which $\varphi$
differs from the formula obtained by retaining only terms of width at most
$\lceil\log_2(\operatorname{size}(\varphi)/\varepsilon)\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Approximation by a narrow DNF]
\lean{FABL.exists_DNF_width_truncation_close}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b001
}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ have a DNF representation with at most $s$ terms, and let
$\varepsilon>0$. There is a sign-valued Boolean function $g$ with a DNF representation
of width at most $\left\lceil\log_2(s/\varepsilon)\right\rceil$ such that the relative
Hamming distance between $f$ and $g$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linearity of Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_sub}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a
subset of the coordinates. The Fourier coefficient of $f-g$ at $S$ equals the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $S$ minus that of $g$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transfer of Fourier concentration]
\lean{FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn.transfer_of_uniformLpNorm_sub_sq_le}
\label{FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn.transfer_of_uniformLpNorm_sub_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_sub, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightOutside, FABL.parseval, FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_two_sq_eq_uniformInner}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f,g:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let
$\\mathcal F$ be any family of subsets of the $n$ coordinates. If the sum of the squared
Fourier coefficients of $f$ over sets outside $\\mathcal F$ is at most $\\varepsilon_1$,
and the square of the uniform $L^2$ norm of $f-g$ is at most $\\varepsilon_2$, then the
sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $g$ over sets outside $\\mathcal F$ is at
most $2(\\varepsilon_1+\\varepsilon_2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function on the binary cube]
\lean{FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\label{FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv}
For a function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$, define its sign-cube function on
$\{\pm1\}^n$ by composing $f$ with the inverse of the coordinatewise sign encoding
$\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{\pm1\}^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binary representation of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction}
\label{FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv}
For a function $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, define its function on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ by
composing $f$ with the coordinatewise sign encoding $\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{\pm1\}^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Converting a Boolean function back]
\lean{FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary_binaryOfBooleanFunction}
\label{FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary_binaryOfBooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction, FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube. Converting $f$ to a function on the binary cube and then
transporting it back to the sign cube recovers $f$ exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inverse binary function conversion]
\lean{FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction_booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\label{FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction_booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction, FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\difficulty{3}
For every $n$ and every function $f$ from the binary cube $\mathbb F_2^n$ to the sign
set $\{-1,1\}$, converting $f$ to a function on the sign cube and then back to the
binary cube recovers $f$ exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sign assigned along a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.requiredSign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.mem_support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.Sign, FABL.signEncode}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004}
Let a path on $n$ coordinates have an assignment in $\mathbb F_2$ or no assignment at
each coordinate, and let its terminal output be a sign. For a coordinate $i$ in the
path's support (the coordinates with an assignment), its required sign is the sign
encoding of the assigned bit at $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Required sign agrees with the assigned bit]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.requiredSign_spec}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.requiredSign, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.Sign, FABL.signEncode, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let a path on $n$ binary coordinates have terminal
output in the sign group $\mathbb{Z}^{\times}$. If coordinate $i$ belongs to the path's
support and its assigned bit is $b\in\mathbb{F}_2$, then the sign required at $i$ is the
sign encoding of $b$, namely $(-1)^b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Literals determined by a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.requiredSign, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
Let a path on $n$ coordinates have an assignment in $\mathbb F_2$ or no assignment at
each coordinate, and a sign-valued terminal output. Associate to it the list containing,
for every coordinate in its support, the literal at that coordinate whose required sign
is the sign encoding of the path's assigned bit there.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Distinct indices in the path literals]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals_nodupIndices}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let a path on $n$ binary coordinates have output in the
sign group $\mathbb{Z}^{\times}$. In the list of literals associated with the path, the
coordinate indices are pairwise distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Path assignment term]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toDNFTerm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals_nodupIndices, FABL.Sign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
For a path on $n$ Boolean coordinates, form the conjunction term whose literals are the
literals determined by the path. The term has no repeated coordinate indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Negated path clause]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toCNFClause}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toLiterals_nodupIndices, FABL.Literal.negate, FABL.Sign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
For a path on $n$ Boolean coordinates, form a term from the path's literals by negating
each literal. The resulting term has no repeated coordinate indices.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let a path on the $n$-dimensional binary cube have a
sign as its terminal label. The width of the DNF term associated with the path equals
the number of coordinates fixed along it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Width of the path CNF clause]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.width_toCNFClause}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let a path on the $n$-dimensional binary cube have a
sign as its terminal label. The width of the CNF clause associated with the path equals
the number of coordinates fixed along it.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path assign either no value or a value in
$\bbr/2\bbr$ to each coordinate, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The DNF term associated with
the path evaluates to $-1$ at $x$ if and only if the binary vector corresponding to $x$
agrees with every value assigned by the path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clause encoding of a path]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.clauseEval_toCNFClause_eq_one_iff}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on the $n$ binary coordinates fix values on
some coordinates, and let $x$ be a sign vector in $\\{-1,1\\}^n$. The clause formed by
negating the literals for the path's fixed coordinates evaluates to $1$ at $x$ if and
only if the binary vector corresponding coordinatewise to $x$ agrees with every value
fixed by the path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision tree DNF formula]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toDNFFormula}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toDNFTerm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.Sign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean coordinates with outputs in $\\{\pm1\}$. Form
a disjunctive normal form whose terms are the path terms for exactly those paths of $T$
whose terminal output is $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Term count of a tree-derived DNF]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.size_toDNFFormula_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toDNFFormula, FABL.Sign}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean
coordinates whose leaves are labeled by signs in $\{\pm1\}$. The number of terms in the
DNF formula associated with $T$ is at most the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[DNF width bounded by tree depth]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.width_toDNFFormula_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.width_le_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.width_toDNFTerm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.path_length_le_depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toDNFFormula, FABL.Sign}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ coordinates with sign-valued leaves. The width of the
disjunctive normal form associated with $T$ is at most the depth of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision tree paths and DNF evaluation]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_toDNFFormula}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.eval_toDNFTerm_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toDNFTerm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toDNFFormula, FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ coordinates with outputs in
$\{ -1,1\}$. For every sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, its associated disjunctive normal
form evaluates to $-1$ at $x$ if and only if there is a path in $T$ ending at output
$-1$ whose prescribed coordinate values agree with the binary vector corresponding to
$x$ under the coordinatewise bijection between $\mathbb{F}_2$ and $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among the
$n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree whose queries use available coordinates
and whose leaves return signs. Then the Boolean function on the sign cube computed by
the DNF formula associated with $T$ equals the function obtained by evaluating $T$ on
the corresponding binary input, with each binary coordinate encoded as a sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[DNF bounds for a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.hasDNFSizeWidth_of_decisionTree}

  {FABL.signValue_neg}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$
coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree that queries only coordinates in $A$ and has
sign-valued outputs. The function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ obtained by evaluating $T$ on the
coordinatewise binary encoding has a disjunctive normal form with at most as many terms
as $T$ has leaves, and with every term containing at most $\mathrm{depth}(T)$ literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[DNF bounds from a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.hasDNFSizeWidth_of_computes}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the Boolean cube
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with sign-valued outputs, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a
Boolean function. If evaluating $T$ on the coordinatewise binary encoding of each sign
vector computes $f$, then $f$ has a disjunctive normal form with at most as many terms
as $T$ has leaves and with every term containing at most $\mathrm{depth}(T)$ literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision tree CNF formula]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toCNFFormula}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.toCNFClause, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.Sign}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean coordinates with outputs in $\{\pm1\}$. Form a
conjunctive normal form whose clauses are obtained by negating the path literals for
exactly those paths of $T$ whose terminal output is $+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Clause count of a tree-derived CNF]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.size_toCNFFormula_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toCNFFormula, FABL.Sign}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean
coordinates whose leaves are labeled by signs in $\{\pm1\}$. The number of clauses in
the CNF formula associated with $T$ is at most the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CNF width bounded by tree depth]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.width_toCNFFormula_le}

}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ coordinates with sign-valued leaves. The width of the
conjunctive normal form associated with $T$ is at most the depth of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on the binary cube with leaves labeled by signs in $\{
-1,1\}$. The Boolean function represented by the CNF formula associated with $T$ agrees
at every sign-cube input with the function obtained by converting that input to binary
coordinates, evaluating $T$, and converting its output to a sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CNF bounds for a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.hasCNFSizeWidth_of_decisionTree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.size_toCNFFormula_le, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toCNFFormula, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.toCNFFormula_toBooleanFunction, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.width_toCNFFormula_le, FABL.HasCNFSizeLE, FABL.HasCNFWidthLE, FABL.Sign, FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b007
}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$
coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree that queries only coordinates in $A$ and has
sign-valued outputs. The function on $\{−1,1\}^n$ obtained by evaluating $T$ on the
coordinatewise binary encoding has a conjunctive normal form with at most as many
clauses as $T$ has leaves, and with every clause containing at most $\mathrm{depth}(T)$
literals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CNF bounds from a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.hasCNFSizeWidth_of_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.hasCNFSizeWidth_of_decisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.HasCNFSizeLE, FABL.HasCNFWidthLE, FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryOfBooleanFunction, FABL.booleanFunctionOfBinary}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the Boolean cube
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with sign-valued outputs, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a
Boolean function. If evaluating $T$ on the coordinatewise binary encoding of each sign
vector computes $f$, then $f$ has a conjunctive normal form with at most as many clauses
as $T$ has leaves and with every clause containing at most $\mathrm{depth}(T)$ literals.
\end{theorem}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\{−1,1\}^n$ to $\{−1,1\}$, let $s,k$ be
natural numbers, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ binary coordinates with
sign-valued leaves. Suppose that evaluating $T$ on the binary encoding of any input
gives the value of $f$, that $T$ has at most $s$ leaves, and that its depth is at most
$k$. Then $f$ has a DNF representation with at most $s$ terms and width at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CNF representation from a decision tree]

\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\{−1,1\}^n$ to $\{−1,1\}$, let $s,k$ be
natural numbers, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ binary coordinates with
sign-valued leaves. Suppose that evaluating $T$ on the binary encoding of any input
gives the value of $f$, that $T$ has at most $s$ leaves, and that its depth is at most
$k$. Then $f$ has a CNF representation with at most $s$ clauses and width at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Initial sorting terms]
\lean{FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrefix}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p094-b001
}
\label{FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.pair}
On three Boolean coordinates, take the list of three conjunction terms with literal
lists $[(0,+1),(2,+1),(1,+1)]$, $[(0,+1),(2,-1)]$, and $[(0,-1),(1,+1),(2,+1)]$, where
each pair records a coordinate and its required sign. Each term has distinct coordinate
indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Printed sorting DNF]
\lean{FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b005}
\label{FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.pair, FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrefix}
On three Boolean coordinates, take the disjunctive normal form whose terms are the
initial sorting terms, followed by the conjunction term with literals $[(1,-1),(2,-1)]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the printed sorting decision tree DNF]
\lean{FABL.size_sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\label{FABL.size_sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\difficulty{1}
The printed DNF associated with the sorting decision tree on three inputs has exactly
four terms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Printed decision tree DNF width]
\lean{FABL.width_sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\label{FABL.width_sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.sort3DecisionTreeDNFPrinted}
\difficulty{1}
The width of the specified printed sort-3 decision-tree disjunctive normal form is
exactly $3$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
On the three-dimensional Boolean cube, the DNF function constructed from the decision
tree for sorting agrees pointwise with the function that returns $-1$ when the three
input bits, obtained by identifying sign $-1$ with true and sign $1$ with false, are in
nondecreasing or nonincreasing order, and returns $1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Involution of Boolean duality]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual_involutive}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual_involutive}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{\\pm1\\}$. Define its
dual by negating both the input and the output. Applying this duality twice returns $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Relative Hamming distance under Boolean duality]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_booleanDual}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.signCubeNegEquiv, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ and $g$ be Boolean functions on the sign cube of dimension $n$. Their relative
Hamming distance is unchanged when both functions are replaced by their Boolean duals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[CNF width truncation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b001
}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
Given a conjunctive normal form $\psi$ and a natural number $w$, retain precisely those
clauses of $\psi$ whose width is at most $w$, preserving their order.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n,w\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $\{-1,1\}^n$. After discarding
every clause of width greater than $w$, the maximum width of the remaining clauses is at
most $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size under width truncation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.size_truncateWidth_le}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.size_truncateWidth_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,w\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $\{-1,1\}^n$. The number of
clauses remaining after retaining only clauses of width at most $w$ is no greater than
the original number of clauses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Switching and width truncation commute]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_truncateWidth}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_truncateWidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr, FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,w\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $\{-1,1\}^n$. Switching its
clauses to DNF terms after retaining clauses of width at most $w$ gives the same DNF
formula as switching first and then retaining terms of width at most $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error after width truncation]
\lean{FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_truncateWidth_le_of_size_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b001
}
\label{FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_truncateWidth_le_of_size_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CNFFormula, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_booleanDual, FABL.CNFFormula.size, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.truncateWidth, FABL.dnfWidthTruncationCutoff, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.relativeHammingDist_truncateWidth_le_of_size_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on the
Boolean cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ with at most $s$ clauses. Retain only clauses of width at most
$\left\lceil\log_2(s/\varepsilon)\right\rceil$ to form a truncated formula. The fraction
of inputs on which the original and truncated formulas differ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Approximation by a narrow CNF]
\lean{FABL.exists_CNF_width_truncation_close}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b001
}
\label{FABL.exists_CNF_width_truncation_close}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.relativeHammingDist_truncateWidth_le_of_size_le, FABL.CNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.truncateWidth, FABL.CNFFormula.width_truncateWidth_le, FABL.HasCNFSizeLE, FABL.HasCNFWidthLE, FABL.dnfWidthTruncationCutoff, FABL.relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ have a CNF representation with at most $s$ clauses, and
let $\varepsilon>0$. There is a sign-valued Boolean function $g$ with a CNF
representation of width at most $\left\lceil\log_2(s/\varepsilon)\right\rceil$ such that
the relative Hamming distance between $f$ and $g$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Negation of a sign value]
\lean{FABL.signValue_neg}
\label{FABL.signValue_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every sign $s$, the real value of its negation is the negative of its real value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative Squares Under Boolean Duality]
\lean{FABL.sq_discreteDerivative_booleanDual}
\label{FABL.sq_discreteDerivative_booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.Sign, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.discreteDerivative_apply, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signCubeNegEquiv, FABL.signValue_neg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. Define
the dual function by $f^*(x)=-f(-x)$, and for a real-valued function $g$ define $D_i
g(x)$ as half the difference between its values at $x$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$
and to $-1$. Then $(D_i f^*(x))^2=(D_i f(-x))^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence under Boolean duality]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_booleanDual}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_booleanDual}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.CNFFormula.booleanDual, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.influence, FABL.signCubeNegEquiv, FABL.sq_discreteDerivative_booleanDual, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean function $f$ on sign vectors of dimension $n$, the total influence of
its Boolean dual equals the total influence of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence bound for bounded-width CNF]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_of_hasCNFWidthLE}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b004
}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_of_hasCNFWidthLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr, FABL.CNFFormula.switchAndOr_toBooleanFunction, FABL.CNFFormula.width, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.DNFFormula.width, FABL.HasCNFWidthLE, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_booleanDual, FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_of_hasDNFWidthLE}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on an $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose it is
computed by a conjunctive normal form whose clauses each contain at most $w$ literals.
Then the total influence of $f$ is at most $2w$.
\end{theorem}
